data.title: Homepage
data.hero_sub: Falling in love with Lake Tahoe is easy. Buying the right home in a market of 10,000 parcels, where one street changes the value and one winter changes the neighborhood, takes someone who has lived it. I have, for 35 years.
data.reality_heading: Incline Village Isn't Like Any Market You've Bought In Before.
data.reality_body: I only work our 10,000 parcels. That's a micro market, and it doesn't follow the trends you'd read about in Reno, the Bay Area, or even Truckee on the other side of the hill. Values change across one street, and a thousand feet of elevation means five times the snow load. I've watched this market from the inside since 1992, and I read it for my clients, on their side of the table.
data.stat1_desc: More closed sales than any other agent in town over that stretch, per Incline Village MLS data. The next agent is at 174.
data.stat2_desc: Sellers here expect a cash offer. A local lender and a clean contract are what let the other 40% compete.
data.stat3_desc: Roughly 700 agents work one small town. I know most of them, and knowing what the other side needs is how offers get accepted here.
data.cta_heading: Every Tahoe Story Starts With One Conversation.
data.cta_body: Buying, selling, or just curious what your place is worth. Call or text the team line and one of us picks up.
data.emotion_h1: Are You Coming to Ski, to Retire, or to Raise a Family?
data.emotion_body: That's the first thing I ask every buyer, before bedrooms or views or price. What are you going to do when you get here? The answer decides the neighborhood, the elevation, the walk to the beach, and whether a condo or a house makes sense. The right home is the one that fits the life you came for.
data.proof_body: One client has done 23 transactions with me. Most of the sellers I list have bought or sold with me before, and this year several came to me after a year with another agent and no sale. That only happens when the advice was honest the first time.
data.micro_heading: Same Zip Code, Very Different Markets
data.insights_body: Notes from inside the market: what's selling, what's stalling, and why the answer changes with the elevation.

data.title: Buyers
data.lead: Many of the most significant properties in Incline Village never see a public listing. Grant's network surfaces them first.
data.card1_p: Direct access to properties before they hit Compass or MLS — from generational lakefront homes to ski-in mountain estates.
data.card2_p: Buyer agency that prioritizes your privacy. NDA-backed showings, blind offers when appropriate.
data.card3_p: Tahoe-specific zoning, water-rights, and TRPA permitting handled before they become deal-killers.
data.card4_p: We help with property managers, contractors, IVGID enrollment, and the hundred small things between purchase and possession.
data.headline: Quiet Access to Tahoe's Most Coveted Estates.

data.title: Sellers
data.lead: Selling Tahoe property is personal. Our process is tailored for sellers who care as much about who buys it as what it sells for.
data.card1_p: Off-market positioning that protects your privacy and the property's storyline.
data.card2_p: Selective staging, photography, and a calibrated price ladder — built around comparable transactions, not algorithms.
data.card3_p: Cash-pre-approval verification, intentions discussion, and lifestyle-fit conversations before a single showing.
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker Global Luxury network places your home in front of the right buyers in Aspen, Jackson, and Park City.
data.headline: A Sale Designed Around Your Life, Not Just the Listing.

data.title: Concierge
data.lead: My work doesn't stop at the closing table. Call the team about anything the house needs and we'll either handle it ourselves or find the person who will.
data.card1_p: Movers, utilities, the storage unit key, a welcome dinner when you arrive. We've parked a client's Rivian in a garage for him, and I still don't know where the massage chair went.
data.card2_p: Plumbers, electricians, the boiler specialist, the mold crew, the handyman who'll pick up after the dog. Years of knowing who shows up, and who doesn't.
data.card3_p: Establishing Nevada residency is a specialty in itself. I connect you to the local CPAs who do it every day, with my own conflicts disclosed up front.
data.card4_p: Snow season, roof shoveling, landscaping, and a set of eyes on the house between visits, from people I'd use on my own home.
data.headline: Nothing Is Too Big or Too Small.

data.title: About
data.lead: From a 16-year-old part-time ski instructor at Diamond Peak to one of the most consistently top-ranked Sierra agents, Grant has built his career on a single bet: that knowing your client matters more than knowing the market.
data.card1_p: Born in Reno. Family moved to Incline in 1989. Helped run his grandfather's small fly-fishing outfit on the East Shore — that's where the relationships started.
data.card2_p: JD from McGeorge School of Law, real-estate-focused. Practiced for four years before moving into agency in 2007.
data.card3_p: "You don't sell Tahoe by selling Tahoe. You sell it by listening for what someone is actually looking for, and then quietly finding it."
data.card4_p: Coldwell Banker International Society of Excellence, six consecutive years. Top 1% of Sierra agents by volume.
data.headline: Three Decades. One Lake. Thousands of Conversations.

data.title: Crystal Bay
data.blurb: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.hero_sub: The state-line gateway, where grand lakefront estates meet original mid-century cabins on wooded lots.
data.overview: Crystal Bay sits where Highway 28 crosses from California into Nevada, wrapping the northwest corner of the lake. It's the quieter, more weathered cousin of Incline Village — a mix of grand lakefront estates and original mid-century cabins on wooded lots, many held by the same families for generations.
data.take: Crystal Bay rewards patience. The lakefront here rarely lists publicly, and when it does the right buyer is often already on a list. If this is the corner you want, the move is to be known here before the home exists.

data.title: Community Page
data.hero_sub: I moved here in 1992 and I'm raising my kids here. These are the neighborhoods, the beaches, the schools, and the history as a resident sees them, with the homes for sale in each one.
data.nb_intro: Tap an area on the map to see its character, or pick a neighborhood below. Each opens its own guide, with the homes currently for sale there.
data.todo_heading: What Living on the North Shore Looks Like
data.todo_intro: Skiing in the morning, the beach by afternoon — the calendar here runs on the seasons.
data.todo1_p: A community-owned ski resort with some of the best lake-view runs on the North Shore — and short lift lines compared with the bigger Tahoe resorts.
data.todo2_p: Incline, Burnt Cedar, and Ski Beach are reserved for residents and their guests — swimming, picnics, and boat access through the summer.
data.todo3_p: The Robert Trent Jones championship course and the shorter mountain course, both run by the community improvement district.
data.todo4_p: Hiking and biking from the village down to the lake, plus the East Shore Trail and Sand Harbor's coves just off Highway 28.
data.todo5_p: Boating, paddleboarding, and kayaking on the clearest large lake in the country, with full-service marinas a short drive away.
data.todo6_p: Captain Whittell's stone lakeside castle south of Sand Harbor, open for docent-led tours through the summer months.
data.quote_text: Every parcel here comes with recreation privileges: the private beaches, Diamond Peak, the golf courses, the rec center. It's the closest thing to a country club membership that arrives with the deed, and I don't know of anywhere else that works this way.
data.quote_cite: Grant C. Meyer · Incline Village since 1992
data.schools_heading: Learning, a Few Minutes From Home
data.schools_body: Incline Village built its first elementary school in 1964 and its high school as the community itself took shape. Today families choose between the local public schools and a handful of private options — all within the village, none more than a short drive away.
data.school2: Private K–8 options within the village
data.school3: A newer elementary campus completed in 2009
data.history_heading: From Logging Camp to Master-Planned Village
data.h1_p: The North Shore began as timber country, feeding the Comstock silver mines of Virginia City. Through the 1800s a narrow-gauge line hauled logs up the mountain to a V-flume — the scars of that era still trace the ridgelines between Mill Creek and Sand Harbor.
data.h2_p: By the early 1900s the lake had become a summer escape. Captain George Whittell bought some 40,000 acres and built a stone castle south of Sand Harbor — the Thunderbird Lodge — where he was known for legendary parties and a private menagerie that included lions and an elephant.
data.h3_p: In the 1960s the Crystal Bay Development Company acquired Whittell's holdings and set out to build a master-planned community. Robert Trent Jones designed the golf course, the name Incline Village was chosen, and the first school opened in 1964 — the framework of the village you see today.
data.living_intro: The practical side of the move — how you get here, what residency opens up, and what the year actually feels like.
data.live1_p:
Reno–Tahoe International Airport sits about 45 minutes down Highway 431, which makes Incline Village one of the more reachable luxury markets in the Sierra.

Sacramento and the Bay Area are an easy weekend drive, and most of the village is only a few minutes from Highway 28 along the shore.
data.live2_p:
The Incline Village General Improvement District runs the private beaches, Diamond Peak, both golf courses, the tennis complex, and the recreation center.

Access comes through an annual recreation fee billed alongside your Washoe County property taxes — one of the things that makes residency here distinct.
data.live3_p:
Incline sits between roughly 6,225 and 7,700 feet, which gives it four genuine seasons: deep, snowy winters and dry, mild summers, with around 290 days of sunshine across the year.

Snow piles up through the winter — well over a hundred inches in a typical year — then gives way to long, clear summers ideal for the lake.
data.live4_p:
The village covers the basics close to home — Raley's and the Village shopping center for groceries, the recreation center and library at the core, and the local public and private schools all within a few minutes.

For specialized care and bigger errands, Tahoe Forest Health System is over the hill in Truckee, and Reno's hospitals and shopping are about 45 minutes away.

data.title: About
data.hero_headline:
You've Found the Place.
Now Find the Right Guide.
data.hero_sub: I've lived in Incline Village since 1992. My clients get someone who is already here, already knows everyone, and isn't going anywhere.
data.why_heading:
Most Agents Work Here.
I Live Here.
data.why_body: After 35 years here I've seen the neighborhoods nobody wanted become the ones everybody wants, and I've seen one big winter send the high-elevation homes to market all at once while the lower ones climbed. None of that shows up in a database. It lives with the people who never left, and I'm one of them.
data.why_quote: I've been a resident in this community for 35 years. You learn who you can count on.
data.stat1_desc: Eighth grade through raising my own two daughters here. Every market cycle, every big winter.
data.stat2_desc: Licensed in 2009. Real estate is my whole profession, and my team of four works it every day of the week.
data.stat3_desc: 181 closed sales in Incline Village since January 2019, more than any other agent in the MLS. Last year I led in both units and dollar volume.
data.guide_heading: 35 Years Here. Still the First One to Pick Up the Phone.
data.cred1_d: Moved here in eighth grade. Raising two daughters here now.
data.cred2_d: Vermont Law School, environmental law. Contracts and land use are where I'm strongest.
data.cred3_d: My father was a general contractor here. I know good bones when I see them.
data.cred4_d: The plumber, the boiler guy, the mold crew. I know who shows up.
data.guide_body: Restaurants came first. My grandfather ran a hamburger stand, and my parents owned two pizza restaurants in Lake Tahoe that I worked as a teenager, ran after college, and was running as COO when we sold them right before I left for law school. That's where I learned customer service: earn someone once, keep them for life. My father spent years as a general contractor in town, so I grew up on job sites too.
data.guide_body2: I studied environmental law at Vermont Law School, in the JD and Master of Science programs, and I put that training to work on every contract, contingency, and land-use question in this basin. I'm not an attorney, but on contracts, negotiation, TRPA coverage rules, and regulatory law I'd put myself in the top fraction of a percent of agents in this industry. Add my father's construction background and 35 years of knowing who to call, and you get someone who can spot good bones, price the fix, and have the right specialist at your house in 90 minutes.
data.pillars_heading: Three Things This Market Does to People Who Don't Know It.
data.pillar1_challenge: A micro market of 10,000 parcels. Two identical floor plans a street apart can sell for very different numbers, and one big winter can send an entire elevation band to market at once. Online estimates run on proximity, and here proximity lies.
data.pillar1_cred: I've lived every cycle here since 1992 and sold here full time since 2009. I work these 10,000 parcels and no others.
data.pillar2_challenge: Impervious coverage, BMP requirements, and TRPA rules exist nowhere else in Nevada, and many agents who dabble in our market can't tell you what they mean for a property. The contract has its own traps: when a contingency waives itself, when earnest money goes hard.
data.pillar2_cred: Law school training. I go through the purchase agreement clause by clause with every client, so you know which lines protect you and which protect the other side.
data.pillar3_challenge: An accepted offer puts us at the 50-yard line. Inspections, appraisal, repairs, title, and a boiler specialist who actually returns calls all stand between you and the keys, and good contractors here are booked for months.
data.pillar3_cred: I know who to call because I've sent them work since 2009 and treated them right. Mold crew at the house in 90 minutes, closed two days later. That's a real one.
data.proof_heading: Nothing Is Too Big or Too Small to Call Me About.
data.proof1_story: A client ran out of gas on Mount Rose Highway. I loaded a five-gallon drum into my Tesla, a car that has never had a drop of gas in it, and drove up the mountain. That's what you do.
data.proof2_story: Before a showing I arranged the movers, packed a client's closet of designer handbags myself, got them into a storage unit, met the movers for the key, and put it in her hand.
data.proof_transition: We're a full concierge operation. I've had my handyman pick up after a client's dog and my landscaper mow the lawn before photos. Call the team, and we'll either do it ourselves or find the person who will.
data.return_heading: When You Buy Here, You're Not a Visitor Anymore.
data.return_body: Incline Village stopped being a place I work a long time ago. My wife Molly and I are raising our two daughters here, in the same town I moved to in eighth grade, and most of my clients turn into the people I see at the market and on the mountain. I've made more real friends through this work than through anything else in my life. I served as president of Incline Village REALTORS in 2023, was named our Realtor of the Year in 2024, and become president of Nevada REALTORS in 2027, because this town and this profession gave me everything.

data.title: Buyers
data.hero_headline: Find Your Place on the North Shore.
data.hero_sub: Are you coming to ski, to retire, to raise a family, or to establish Nevada residency? That's my first question, because the answer decides everything else. Start there, and I'll show you how this market really works.
data.stakes_heading: Out-of-Market Instincts Cost Real Money Here.
data.stakes_p1: Incline Village and Crystal Bay don't behave like the market you're coming from, where an online estimate lands close to the truth and a confident buyer can handle a purchase alone.
data.stakes_p2: In 2021 a couple bought a home here directly from the owner for $3.88 million, no agent, sure they were saving money. They tried to sell two years later. It took three and a half years, and the home closed this year at $1.92 million. Less than half.
data.stakes_p3: This is a micro market of 10,000 parcels, and it moves on a handful of sales. The same floor plan can be worth a very different number one street over, and one hard winter can send a whole elevation band to market at once.
data.stakes_quote: You can avoid making those 50-60% mistakes by paying 3-6%. In our market, that's a fantastic insurance policy.
data.network_heading: The Network You Inherit on Day One.
data.network_p1: This is a resort market. There's no Home Depot in Incline Village, the good contractors are booked for months, and the right specialist isn't in the phone book unless you already know who to call.
data.network_p2: Since 2009 I've been sending work to the trades, lenders, title officers, inspectors, and appraisers who do it right, and treating them right, so they pick up when I call. In a small town everyone earns a reputation fast, good or bad, and I know which plumber to call and which one to avoid. My clients inherit all of that the day they close.
data.network_story: A buyer's inspector flagged mold at the last minute and the sale was about to fall apart. I called my mold guy, he was treating the house within 90 minutes, and we closed two days later. That's what those phone calls are worth.
data.network_quote: It took me 35 years to earn those phone calls. The day you close, every one of them is yours too.
data.tax_body: Nevada is one of the most tax-friendly states in the country. The state charges no personal income tax and no business tax, capital gains aren't taxed at the state level either, and property taxes stay low because Nevada doesn't reassess to your purchase price the way most states do. For buyers coming from California, and lately from Washington, crossing the state line can change the financial picture as much as the house does.
data.tax_turn: What that means for you depends on why you're moving.
data.tax1_kicker: Retiring here, or planning your estate
data.tax1_title: Keep what you spent a career building.
data.tax1_body:
Nevada charges no personal income tax. Your pension, 401(k) withdrawals, Social Security, and investment income keep their full value at the state level.

There's also no state estate or inheritance tax. When you pass your home and assets to your children or grandchildren, Nevada takes none of it. (Federal estate tax rules still apply, so your estate planner is still worth a call.)

For anyone who spent a career building wealth, that combination is the difference between preserving an estate and watching it shrink a little more every year.
data.tax2_kicker: Earning at the top of your career
data.tax2_title: Income earned as a resident is not taxed by the state.
data.tax2_body:
A high salary or a strong year of capital gains lands very differently here. Against California's top rate, the gap is large enough to factor into where you choose to live.

The part worth understanding: the benefit follows residency, not the deed. To claim it, you make Nevada your true home, where you live, vote, and spend your time. Plenty of people make exactly that move to Incline Village, and a local CPA can walk you through what genuine residency requires.
data.tax3_title: A structure built to keep overhead low.
data.tax3_body: Nevada earned its business-friendly reputation, and the structure backs it up:
data.tax3_bullets:
No corporate income tax
No franchise tax
No gross receipts tax for most businesses (a Commerce Tax applies only above $4M in Nevada revenue)
No inventory tax
Strong legal protection for company directors and officers
A high degree of privacy for business owners
data.tax3_after: For an entrepreneur relocating a company, or running one from a home office above the lake, those add up to lower overhead and fewer state-level headaches. Whether to restructure an entity in Nevada is a decision for your CPA and attorney, and I'm glad to point you toward local professionals who handle it.
data.tax4_title: Low property taxes, and one fee that opens the lake.
data.tax4_body:
Property taxes in Nevada are low by national standards, and well below what most of our buyers leave behind. Nevada also doesn't reassess to your purchase price, so the bill stays low long after you close.

Incline Village is an unincorporated community of Washoe County. Water and sewer service, the private beaches, Diamond Peak Ski Resort, the championship golf courses, the tennis complex, and the recreation center are all managed by the Incline Village General Improvement District (IVGID). Every parcel comes with recreation privileges, which is the closest thing to a country club membership that arrives with the deed.
data.tax_disclaimer: This is general information, not tax or legal advice, and every situation is different. Before you count on any of it, sit down with a local CPA. I send clients to Ashley Quinn CPAs here in town, who specialize in establishing Nevada residency, and in full disclosure they handle my own personal and business taxes as well.
data.investment_heading: Your Home Here Is Also a Portfolio Decision.
data.investment_p1: Almost every buyer I work with treats a purchase here as an investment, even when it's the home they plan to raise a family in. I work the same way. One client has done 23 transactions with me: bought roughly a dozen properties, sold a dozen, kept one, and netted more than $5 million along the way.
data.investment_p2: Construction here is a nightmare, so nearly every buyer wants turnkey and remodeled homes sell at a big premium, which leaves real equity for the buyer willing to take on a project with the right people guiding it. I grew up on my father's job sites, so I can spot good bones and give you an honest estimate of what it takes, which is 50% more time and 50% more money than you're budgeting. Some streets will return every dollar you put in and some never will, and I'll tell you which one you're standing on.
data.investment_quote: I'm less of a realtor and more of a real estate portfolio advisor. Most of my clients are as smart as I am or smarter. My job is to give them the right information, and when I do, they make the right decisions.
data.comm_heading: I Know Both Block by Block.
data.comm_lead: Incline Village and Crystal Bay each have their own character, pricing, and quirks. The sun in February, the walk to dinner, the months you'll spend shoveling: all of it changes by neighborhood, and my notes on each are on the community pages.
data.comm1_desc: The beaches, Diamond Peak, the golf and tennis, and the subdivisions I've watched trade since 1992. Even across one street the values can be very different.
data.comm2_desc: Quieter, more wooded, right at the state line, with its own pricing logic. I read the lakefront and the hillside lots block by block.
data.process_heading: What Working With Me Actually Looks Like.
data.process_body: The first call is about what you're going to do when you get here, what you're using the property for, and whether you're paying cash or financing. Then I teach you the town, because most of my buyers come from out of the area: the neighborhoods, what a thousand feet of elevation does to a winter, what every parcel's IVGID recreation privileges include, and the Nevada tax picture.
data.process_promise: When you're ready, I show you what's on the market now, not just what sold six months ago, because in a micro market that's what sets the price. I call the listing agent before we write, to find out what matters to their seller, so our offer wins on terms that cost you nothing. An accepted offer puts us at the 50-yard line: inspections at whatever depth you want, a local lender for the 40% who finance (sellers here trust them), the appraisal, repairs, title, and then utilities, movers, and dinner on me when you get the keys.
data.cta_heading: Ready to Buy in Tahoe the Right Way?
data.cta_body: Reaching out commits you to nothing. The first conversation is about your goals, your timeline, and whether Tahoe is even the right move. Call or text the team line and one of the four of us picks up.
data.stakes_p4: That knowledge doesn't live in a database. I've been reading this market from inside it since 1992, and I read it for you, on your side of the table.
data.process_body2: We look online first, then you come up and we caravan past the school, the softball fields, and the restaurants you can walk to from one street but not the next. Nobody gets pressured; some buyers decide in a weekend and some take years, and I keep sending listings either way.

data.title: Sellers
data.hero_headline: Your Home's Value Here Isn't What an Algorithm Says It Is.
data.hero_sub: In our most desirable neighborhoods, an original 1962 house sits next door to brand-new construction, and the algorithm averages them. That's why internet estimates are notoriously wrong in this town. I've sold more property in Incline Village than any other agent since 2019, and I price based on what buyers are looking at today. Start with what your home is actually worth.
data.pricing_heading: The Hardest Number to Get Right in This Market.
data.pricing_p1: Pricing here isn't a formula. I start where an appraiser would, with price per square foot and what closed in the last six months, and then I show you something most agents skip: what a buyer for your type of property has on the shelf right now. Six new listings below you make last spring's comps irrelevant, and nothing on the market within $200,000 of you means we can push higher than we could six months ago.
data.pricing_p2: The internet gets this town wrong for a specific reason. Most markets value by proximity, and here proximity means little: an original 1962 home and new construction share a lot line in our best neighborhoods, so the algorithm overvalues one and undervalues the other.
data.pricing_p3: My job is to give you what I know. You get to drive the ship.  Some sellers need to be gone this season, and some are happy to wait years for their number. I'll tell you honestly which price gets which result, and I'll be in this business for another 19 years, so I'm not in a hurry either.
data.pricing_quote: I sell more property than anybody else here, and I still can't promise you a number. The market tells us whether we're priced right. My job is to make sure you hear it early and clearly.
data.timing_heading: The Sellers Who Win Here Are Ready Before the Buyers Arrive.
data.timing_p1: Buyers are here before sellers are ready. They come up to ski in the winter and start looking in April and May, while most owners are still in Arizona, Las Vegas, or Palm Springs and haven't been up to get the house ready for summer.
data.timing_p2: So we list earlier in the spring than most, and we sell a lot of property before the competition shows up. Last winter was mild, so we brought new listings on in November while everyone else had pulled theirs in October, and we got full price, all cash, multiple offers because we watched the weather instead of the calendar.
data.timing_p3: We brought a remodeled three-bedroom condo to market in early spring and set the complex record at $715,000. By late summer, every neighbor who saw that number had listed, and I got a different client a nicer three-bedroom in the same complex for $100,000 less. Same building, one season apart, and my clients were on the right side of both.
data.timing_quote: When I've got a seller who's ready and the marketing package is done, we come on before everyone else lists. That's a real opportunity, and most agents miss it because they're doing what they did last year.
data.mkt_heading: Every Listing Gets the Full Package, Whatever the Price.
data.mkt_p1: It disappoints me how many agents in this industry shoot a $4 million house on an iPhone. Every one of my listings gets professional photography, drone, video, and its own individual property webpage, whatever the price point. Most of our buyers see the home first on a screen from hundreds of miles away, and that first look has to be its best.
data.mkt_p2: Before the camera arrives, my stager sets the home up to show as clean and beautiful as it can. Then the property gets a champagne brunch broker tour so the 700 agents in town see it, open houses, and a QR-code e-flyer on the sign instead of a box of paper that gets snowed on. One of my team members accompanies every showing we can, even on a $500,000 condo, because we know the property better than the buyer's agent walking in the door.
data.reach_body: Through Coldwell Banker Select and the Coldwell Banker Global Luxury network, the listing goes out to a national and international buyer base on top of our local MLS, so a home in Incline Village shows up in front of the relocating buyer in San Francisco and the family flying in from Seattle.
data.network_heading: The Network That Gets Your Home Sale-Ready.
data.network_p1: In a resort market, the good contractors are booked for months, and the right specialist isn't in the phone book unless you already know who to call. I've been building those relationships since 2009, and a seller inherits them the moment we sign.
data.network_p2: When a home needs work before it shows well, I know who to bring in and roughly what it should cost, because I grew up on my father's job sites. A remodel here takes about 50% longer and costs 50% more than it would in most markets, because materials come up the mountain and good contractors are booked months out. Before you spend a dollar getting ready to list, I'll tell you which fixes earn their money back and which to skip.
data.network_story: One of my sellers lives in Australia, and the buyers' inspector flagged the heating system. He couldn't understand it; he skis here every winter, and the heat works fine. Most plumbers won't touch a hydronic boiler, so I got a boiler specialist out, the inspector came back and signed off, and we closed.
data.network_quote: We live in a resort market. It's really hard to get an electrician to your house. So you take care of people. When you treat them right, they treat you right.
data.honesty_heading: I'd Rather Keep You for Life Than Win One Listing.
data.honesty_p1: Too many agents give a seller the answer that wins the listing instead of the truth. I'll be honest even when it isn't what you want to hear, because the business I've built runs on people coming back. One client has done 23 transactions with me, and several of this year's sales were homes that sat unsold with another agent last year.
data.honesty_quote: Penny-wise and pound-foolish happens more than you'd think, and it's why I give you the honest read first and let you drive.
data.honesty_p2: A plumber I work with inherited his father's house and had an off-market offer in hand from an agent the family knew. I walked it, ran the numbers, and told him I thought we could get half a million more. The family wanted to save 3% by not listing; we listed, and they cleared $550,000 more than the offer, 46% more, after paying the commission they'd been trying to avoid.
data.process_heading: What Listing With Me Actually Looks Like.
data.process_body: It starts with me at your house. I can run numbers on square footage from my desk, but your version of remodeled, mine, and a buyer's are three different things, and "lake view" has several categories in our MLS, so I need boots on the ground before we talk price. Then we go through the listing agreement clause by clause, so you know exactly what a contingency does to your deal and when a buyer's earnest money becomes non-refundable. From there it's prep, photography, the property website, the broker tour, and to market on the right timing, with one of my team at every showing we can make.
data.process_promise: When offers come in, I give you the information, and you choose the route. You're driving the train, and my job is to tell you which track gets you there fastest. Under contract, I handle the buyer's inspectors and appraiser, get contractor bids on anything they flag, protect your deposit through escrow, and show up at your signing, because escrow is neutral and I'm not. My job doesn't end when the keys change hands. Movers, utilities, whatever you left behind: we'll either handle it ourselves or find someone who will. Nothing is too small to ask.
data.val_heading: Start With What Your Home Is Worth.
data.val_lead: Give me the address and a little about the place, and I'll come back to you with a real read on value and timing, from comps and from what's on the market against you today. There's no automated number at the end of this form and no pitch, just a read from someone who sells more here than anyone. If you'd like, we'll set a time for me to walk the property.
data.val_success: Thanks. One of the team will be in touch shortly with a first read and a time to talk.
data.val_reassure: Plenty of the owners who call me have several properties and are still deciding how many more winters they want, so a first conversation commits you to nothing. "Not this year" is a perfectly good answer.

data.pricing_p2b: The county records add another wrinkle. Square footage was measured loosely here for decades, so I get an appraisal measurement on almost every listing and market the real number.
